summary: Iteration 7 - Validated the new Analytics module end-to-end. Added /app/backend/tests/test_analytics.py (27 pytest cases). Total backend suite is now 138 passing / 0 failing in ~18.5s (111 carry-over + 27 new). All 5 analytics endpoints behave correctly: /overview returns flat JSON with correct types and matches /api/events count (total_events=20, total_area_affected=4841.6); /countries sorted DESC by event_count with country ASC tie-break, totals match overview; /event-types ALWAYS returns 7-entry zero-filled taxonomy sorted DESC; /severity returns an object with canonical key order low->medium->high->critical (all 4 keys, zero-filled); /trends supports day|week|month with day/week buckets day-aligned UTC and month buckets aligned to day=1, totals match across intervals, invalid interval -> 400 invalid_interval, start>end -> 400 invalid_range, future-only range -> {series:[]}, both 'Z' and '+00:00' ISO formats accepted. /api/modules/analytics now correctly reports status='active' with all 5 capabilities='live'. Frontend smoke (against the correct preview URL https://deforest-monitor-1.preview.emergentagent.com): login works, dashboard renders 20 events with severity bar (Low=5, Medium=5, High=6, Critical=4) and 4841.6 ha total, /map renders 20/20 markers, zero console errors. Repository genuinely uses MongoDB aggregation pipelines ($group, $sort, $cond, $avg, $dateTrunc with timezone='UTC'). Circular-import note honored: analytics/__init__.py imports only repository+service; server.py imports the router directly.

minor.issue: Carry-over: returns 200 with not_found payload instead of 404.

frontend_issues.infra_note: The URL passed to me in earlier runs (forestlens.preview.emergentagent.com) shows the 'Preview Unavailable' overlay; the actual REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL is https://deforest-monitor-1.preview.emergentagent.com and that one works perfectly. No FE changes were expected this iteration; verified nothing regressed.

critical_code_review_comments: analytics_repository.py uses pure MongoDB aggregation pipelines ($group, $sort, $cond, $avg, $dateTrunc) — no Python-side aggregation. Verified.
Overview pipeline computes open/resolved/investigating via $cond inside $sum — correct, single pass over the collection.
by_country and by_event_type pipelines sort by event_count DESC then _id ASC ({'event_count': -1, '_id': 1}) — exactly what the contract requires; tie-break test passes.

Service-layer zero-fills the FULL event-type taxonomy from EVENT_TYPES (single source of truth in app/models/enums.py) AND applies a stable secondary sort by event_type — guarantees deterministic chart axes.
by_severity returns a dict keyed in SEVERITY_ORDER = ('low','medium','high','critical') — Python 3.7+ preserves insertion order so the JSON output respects the canonical order. Verified end-to-end.
Trends pipeline uses $dateTrunc with timezone='UTC' — produces tz-correct day/week/month boundaries on Mongo 5.0+ (we run 7.0.34).

ensure_utc on start_date/end_date in the service guarantees consistent comparisons in $match regardless of whether the client sent 'Z' or '+00:00'. Verified both formats produce identical bucket sums.
AppError('invalid_interval'|'invalid_range', status_code=400) is raised by the service BEFORE touching Mongo — saves a needless round-trip and gives a stable error code to the FE.

analytics/__init__.py intentionally does NOT eagerly import analytics_routes to avoid the routes->deps->module circular import; server.py imports the router directly. Comment in __init__.py captures the gotcha — good defensive doc.
Routes use Depends(get_current_user) on every endpoint — auth requirement verified across all 5 (returns 401 unauthenticated).
Float rounding helper _r() coerces None->0.0 — overview total_area_affected never returns null even on an empty collection.
average_confidence is rounded to 3 decimals (_r(value, 3)) — matches contract.

Suggestion (minor): /analytics/trends has no default for start_date/end_date (FastAPI Query(...) means required). Consider a sensible 30-day default to make the endpoint friendlier from a chart that's first rendering — not blocking.

Suggestion (minor): /analytics/trends doesn't pad missing buckets with zero — clients have to LOCF/zero-fill themselves. The TEST does NOT require this, but for chart UX it would be a nice future extension.
seed_data_creation: None. Tests rely on the 20 ForestEvents seeded by the startup hook. Synthetic trend events are not needed because the existing seeded events already span ~30 days, which is enough to exercise day vs week vs month bucketing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml (138 tests, ~18.5s). New test file is /app/backend/tests/test_analytics.py with classes: TestModuleInfo, TestAuthRequired (5 parametrized), TestOverview (3), TestByCountry, TestByEventType, TestBySeverity, TestTrends (6: day_shape, week_and_month_consistent, invalid_interval, invalid_range, future_empty, both ISO formats), TestRegressionSmoke (9 parametrized). KEY GOTCHAS: (1) AppError JSON shape is {'detail': '<msg>', 'code': '<code>'} — detail is a STRING not a dict. (2) The trends route requires start_date+end_date as Query(...) — they have no defaults, so calling without them returns 422. (3) Severity endpoint returns an OBJECT (not array) and Python dict insertion order makes the canonical low->medium->high->critical order visible in JSON. (4) /analytics/event-types ALWAYS returns 7 entries regardless of whether some types have zero events. (5) Trends comparison test fetches the same range at day/week/month intervals and asserts len(month)<=len(week)<=len(day) AND sum(event_count) equal across all three intervals — a robust invariant that doesn't depend on seed randomness. (6) Frontend public URL is https://deforest-monitor-1.preview.emergentagent.com (NOT forestlens.preview.emergentagent.com which is some stale ref). Login UI fields are input[type=email] and input[type=password] + button[type=submit]; no data-testid on the login form (carry-over).
rca_of_the_issue: N/A - no bugs found. The Analytics module is implemented correctly and matches the request spec. The single test I authored that initially failed (test_invalid_interval) was a TEST-side mistake on my part — I assumed body['detail'] could be a dict; the actual API returns it as a string with a separate top-level 'code' field. Fixed the test, no code changes needed.
